revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Painting a Bedroom
revealWordProblem.text: Tahira is planning to paint the walls of her bedroom, which is in the shape of a rectangular prism 12 ft long, 10 ft wide, and 8 ft tall. She will not paint the floor or ceiling. The room has one window (3 ft by 4 ft) and two doors (each 3 ft by 7 ft) that will not be painted. How many square feet of wall does Tahira need to paint?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Wall area = perimeter × height = 2(12 + 10) × 8 = 44 × 8 = 352 ft². Subtract the openings: window = 3 × 4 = 12 ft²; two doors = 2 × (3 × 7) = 42 ft². Paintable area = 352 − 12 − 42 = 298 ft².

turnAndTalk.question: Your class is painting two capsule shapes: a rectangular prism and a triangular prism. How is finding the surface area of each shape the same, and how is it different?
turnAndTalk.kernel: For both, you add the areas of all the faces, but the shapes and number of faces differ.

turnAndTalk.question: A classmate wrote SA = 2(12×7) + 2(12×5) + (7×5) = 323 cm² for a 12 × 7 × 5 prism. How do you find and fix their mistake?

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students notice the missing '2' on the last pair, compute 2(7×5) = 70, and correct the total to 168 + 120 + 70 = 358 cm².
turnAndTalk.extend: What general rule about prism faces does this error break, and how could the net help a student avoid it?

conceptIntro.heading: How do we find the surface area of a prism?
conceptIntro.intro: Surface area is the total area of all the faces of a solid. A rectangular prism has 6 faces; a triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles). Add every face to get the total.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: No matter the prism, find the area of every face and add them all together.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My triangular prism has triangle bases (base 6 in., height 4 in.), is 10 in. long, and the two slant sides are 5 in. each.
Each triangle base is ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, and there are 2 of them: 2 × 12 = 24.
Now the 3 rectangles: 6 × 10 = 60, 5 × 10 = 50, and 5 × 10 = 50, which add to 160.
I add the bases and the rectangles: 24 + 160 = 184.
So the surface area is 184 in². I counted 5 faces because it is a triangular prism.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a rectangular prism: 5 long, 4 wide, 3 tall. How many faces does it have?
Top and bottom: 5 × 4 = 20, times 2 = 40. Front and back: 5 × 3 = 15, times 2 = 30.
Left and right: 4 × 3 = 12, times 2 = 24. Now add 40 + 30 + 24. What is the surface area?
Yes, SA = 94 cm². Surface area always uses square units.

optional.stem: A rectangular time capsule box measures 3 in by 4 in by 5 in. How much wrapping paper covers its surface (no overlap)?
choiceFeedback: That's the volume — surface area needs the sum of all six face areas, not length × width × height.
You found the sum of three face areas but forgot each face has a matching opposite one.
Check the units — a wrapped surface is measured in square units, not cubic.
optional.stemEs: Una caja rectangular para una cápsula del tiempo mide 3 in por 4 in por 5 in. ¿Cuánto papel de envolver cubre su superficie (sin traslape)?
hints: Wrapping paper covers the outside of the box, so this asks for surface area, not volume — the answer will be in square inches.
A rectangular prism has 3 different face sizes, and each size appears twice. Find those three different face areas first.
The three face areas are 3 × 4, 3 × 5, and 4 × 5. Work each one out, then double every result and add them.
hintsEs: El papel cubre el exterior de la caja, así que se pide el área de superficie, no el volumen: la respuesta va en pulgadas cuadradas.
Un prisma rectangular tiene 3 tamaños distintos de cara, y cada tamaño aparece dos veces. Primero halla esas tres áreas distintas.
Las tres áreas son 3 × 4, 3 × 5 y 4 × 5. Calcula cada una, luego duplica cada resultado y súmalos.

optional.stem: A rectangular capsule crate is 6 cm long, 5 cm wide, and 4 cm tall. How much cardboard is needed to cover all its faces?
choiceFeedback: That's the volume calculation — surface area needs the sum of all six face areas instead.
You added three face areas but forgot each one has a matching opposite face to double.
Check the units — covering a surface uses square units, not cubic units.
optional.stemEs: Una caja rectangular para cápsulas mide 6 cm de largo, 5 cm de ancho y 4 cm de alto. ¿Cuánto cartón se necesita para cubrir todas sus caras?
hints: Covering all the faces means finding surface area — the total area of the outside, measured in square centimeters.
Pair the faces up: front and back, left and right, top and bottom. Each pair holds two identical rectangles.
Find the three face areas 6 × 5, 6 × 4, and 5 × 4. Double each one, then add the three doubled amounts together.
hintsEs: Cubrir todas las caras significa hallar el área de superficie: el área total del exterior, medida en centímetros cuadrados.
Empareja las caras: frente y atrás, izquierda y derecha, arriba y abajo. Cada par tiene dos rectángulos iguales.
Halla las tres áreas 6 × 5, 6 × 4 y 5 × 4. Duplica cada una y luego suma las tres cantidades duplicadas.

optional.stem: A triangular prism is 10 in long. Its triangle ends have base 8 in, height 6 in, and sides 8, 6, and 10 in. Find its surface area.
optional.explanation: Two triangle ends: 2 × (½ × 8 × 6) = 48 in². Three rectangles: (8 + 6 + 10) × 10 = 24 × 10 = 240 in². SA = 48 + 240 = 288 in².
choiceFeedback: You found the rectangular sides but forgot to add the two triangular ends.
You found the triangular ends but forgot to add the three rectangular sides.
Check the units — wrapping a surface uses square units, not cubic.
optional.stemEs: Un prisma triangular mide 10 in de largo. Sus extremos triangulares tienen base 8 in, altura 6 in y lados de 8, 6 y 10 in. Halla su área de superficie.
optional.explanationEs: Dos extremos triangulares: 2 × (½ × 8 × 6) = 48 in². Tres rectángulos: (8 + 6 + 10) × 10 = 24 × 10 = 240 in². Área de superficie = 48 + 240 = 288 in².
hints: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangles on the ends and 3 rectangles wrapping around the sides.
Find the two triangle areas with ½ × base × height, then find each rectangle as one triangle side times the length of the prism.
One triangle is ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in², so the two ends together are 48 in². Now handle the rectangles: each side of the triangle (8, 6, and 10) times the 10 in length.
hintsEs: Un prisma triangular tiene 5 caras: 2 triángulos en los extremos y 3 rectángulos que lo rodean.
Halla las áreas de los dos triángulos con ½ × base × altura, y luego halla cada rectángulo como un lado del triángulo por el largo del prisma.
Un triángulo es ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in², así que los dos extremos juntos dan 48 in². Ahora trabaja los rectángulos: cada lado del triángulo (8, 6 y 10) por el largo de 10 in.

optional.instructions: Find each prism's surface area. Then sort it by whether it needs 96 in² of paper or less, or more than 96 in².
optional.hint: Surface area = the total of all the faces. Compare each result to 96 in².
optional.explanation: Paper wraps the outside, so compare each surface area to 96 in². The 3×4×5 capsule needs 94 in² and the 4×4×4 cube needs exactly 96 in², so both fit in the first bin, while the 6×5×4 capsule at 148 in² and the triangular capsule at 288 in² are over 96 in².
optional.explanationEs: El papel envuelve el exterior, así que compara cada área de superficie con 96 in². La cápsula de 3×4×5 necesita 94 in² y el cubo de 4×4×4 necesita exactamente 96 in², así que las dos van en el primer grupo, mientras que la cápsula de 6×5×4 con 148 in² y la cápsula triangular con 288 in² pasan de 96 in².
optional.instructionsEs: Encuentra el área superficial de cada prisma. Después clasifícalo según si necesita 96 in² de papel o menos, o más de 96 in².

optional.label: Match each rectangular capsule's dimensions to how much cardboard wraps its surface.
optional.hint: Add the areas of all six faces to find how much cardboard wraps each box.
optional.explanation: Cardboard wraps all six faces, so each match is SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh: 7×3×2 gives 42 + 28 + 12 = 82 in², 6×4×2 gives 48 + 24 + 16 = 88 in², 9×2×2 gives 36 + 36 + 8 = 80 in², and 6×5×3 gives 60 + 36 + 30 = 126 in². Notice the long, skinny 9×2×2 box needs the least cardboard even though it is the longest.
optional.explanationEs: El cartón envuelve las seis caras, así que cada pareja es SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh: 7×3×2 da 42 + 28 + 12 = 82 in², 6×4×2 da 48 + 24 + 16 = 88 in², 9×2×2 da 36 + 36 + 8 = 80 in² y 6×5×3 da 60 + 36 + 30 = 126 in². Fíjate en que la caja larga y delgada de 9×2×2 necesita menos cartón aunque sea la más larga.
optional.labelEs: Empareja las dimensiones de cada cápsula rectangular con cuánto cartón envuelve su superficie.

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: Rectangular capsule: l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 2 in. Find the wrapping paper (surface area).
workedExample.workEs: Cápsula rectangular: l = 4 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 2 pulg. Encuentra el papel de regalo (área superficial).

workedExample.label: Formula
workedExample.work: Surface area means adding the area of all 6 faces: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh.
workedExample.workEs: El área superficial suma el área de las 6 caras: SA = 2la + 2lh + 2ah.

workedExample.label: Calculate
workedExample.work: The student multiplied the three dimensions: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24, so they wrote SA = 24 in².
workedExample.workEs: El estudiante multiplicó las tres dimensiones: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24, así que escribió SA = 24 in².

optional.correctWork: Multiplying l × w × h gives the VOLUME (24 in³), not the surface area. To wrap the box you must add all six faces: SA = 2(4×3) + 2(4×2) + 2(3×2) = 24 + 16 + 12 = 52 in².
hints: Wrapping paper covers the outside faces — that is surface area, not how much fits inside.
Multiplying l × w × h gives volume in cubic units. Surface area adds 6 faces: 2(4×3) + 2(4×2) + 2(3×2) = 52 in².
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — confusión con el papel de regalo
optional.explanation: In the Calculate step the student multiplied 4 × 3 × 2, which measures how much fits inside — the volume, 24 in³. Wrapping paper covers the outside faces, so add all six: 2(4×3) + 2(4×2) + 2(3×2) = 24 + 16 + 12 = 52 in².
optional.explanationEs: En el paso de calcular, el estudiante multiplicó 4 × 3 × 2, lo que mide cuánto cabe dentro: el volumen, 24 in³. El papel de regalo cubre las caras exteriores, así que suma las seis: 2(4×3) + 2(4×2) + 2(3×2) = 24 + 16 + 12 = 52 in².
optional.correctWorkEs: Multiplicar l × a × h da el VOLUMEN (24 in³), no el área superficial. Para envolver la caja debes sumar las seis caras: SA = 2(4×3) + 2(4×2) + 2(3×2) = 24 + 16 + 12 = 52 in².

approaching.stem: What is the surface area of a rectangular prism with l = 5 cm, w = 4 cm, h = 3 cm?
choiceFeedback: That's the volume — surface area adds up all six face areas instead of multiplying three edges.
Check the units — a surface measurement needs square units, not cubic.
You found half the faces — remember each face has a matching opposite face to double.
hints: You need surface area — the total of all 6 face areas of the 5 × 4 × 3 prism — not the space inside.
Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh: three different faces, each with a matching twin on the opposite side.
Find the three face areas first: 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15, and 4×3 = 12. Double each, then add the results.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de superficie de un prisma rectangular con l = 5 cm, w = 4 cm, h = 3 cm?
hintsEs: Necesitas el área superficial: el total de las 6 áreas de cara del prisma de 5 × 4 × 3, no el espacio de adentro.
Usa AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah: tres caras distintas, cada una con su gemela en el lado opuesto.
Halla primero las tres áreas de cara: 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15 y 4×3 = 12. Duplica cada una y luego suma los resultados.

approaching.stem: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
approaching.explanation: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangular bases and 3 rectangular lateral faces.
choiceFeedback: Count again — a triangular prism has more rectangular sides than that, plus its two ends.
That's the face count for a rectangular prism — a triangular prism has one fewer face.
That's just the rectangular sides — don't forget the two triangular ends.
hints: Picture a tent or a triangular chocolate box: two triangle ends plus rectangles wrapping around the sides.
Count the two triangular bases first, then count one rectangle for each side of the triangle.
A triangle has 3 sides, so count 3 rectangular faces. Then add the triangular ends to that count.
approaching.explanationEs: Un prisma triangular tiene 5 caras: 2 bases triangulares y 3 caras laterales rectangulares.
hintsEs: Imagina una tienda de campaña o una caja triangular de chocolates: dos extremos triangulares más rectángulos que envuelven los lados.
Cuenta primero las dos bases triangulares y luego cuenta un rectángulo por cada lado del triángulo.
Un triángulo tiene 3 lados, así que cuenta 3 caras rectangulares. Luego suma los extremos triangulares a ese conteo.

approaching.stem: A triangular prism has two triangular bases each with area 12 cm² and three rectangular faces with areas 30 cm², 40 cm², and 40 cm². What is the total surface area?
choiceFeedback: You added the three rectangles but left out both triangular bases.
You included only one triangular base — a prism has two matching triangular ends to add.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: All five face areas are given: two triangles of 12 cm² each, and rectangles of 30, 40, and 40 cm².
Total surface area = every face added once — count BOTH triangular bases, not just one.
Start with the triangles: 2 × 12 = 24 cm². Then add the three rectangle areas to that.
approaching.stemEs: Un prisma triangular tiene dos bases triangulares, cada una con un área de 12 cm², y tres caras rectangulares con áreas de 30 cm², 40 cm² y 40 cm². ¿Cuál es el área de superficie total?
hintsEs: Te dan las cinco áreas de cara: dos triángulos de 12 cm² cada uno y rectángulos de 30, 40 y 40 cm².
Área superficial total = cada cara sumada una vez; cuenta AMBAS bases triangulares, no solo una.
Empieza con los triángulos: 2 × 12 = 24 cm². Luego súmale las tres áreas de los rectángulos.

approaching.label: Put the steps in order for finding the surface area of a triangular prism.

categories.label: Steps in order (first → last)
items: Find the area of one triangular base
Multiply the triangle area by 2 (two bases)
Find the area of each rectangular lateral face
Add all three rectangle areas together
Add the two triangle areas + all rectangle areas = SA

approaching.hint: Think about the order of steps for finding a triangular prism's surface area.
hints: The cards describe finding a triangular prism's SA: triangles first, then rectangles, then a final total.
Order it like building a net: one triangle's area, double it, each rectangle's area, add rectangles, combine all.
Place 'Find the area of one triangular base' first — you need one triangle before you can double it.
approaching.explanation: A triangular prism has 5 faces, so the steps go triangles first, then rectangles, then a total: find one triangular base, double it for the two bases, find each rectangular lateral face, add those three rectangles, and finally add the triangles and rectangles together. Doubling the triangle before moving on keeps the two identical bases from being forgotten.
approaching.explanationEs: Un prisma triangular tiene 5 caras, así que los pasos van primero con los triángulos, luego con los rectángulos y al final con el total: halla una base triangular, duplícala para las dos bases, halla el área de cada cara rectangular lateral, suma esos tres rectángulos y al final suma los triángulos y los rectángulos. Duplicar el triángulo antes de seguir evita que olvides una de las dos bases iguales.
approaching.labelEs: Ordena los pasos para encontrar el área superficial de un prisma triangular.
hintsEs: Las tarjetas describen hallar el AS de un prisma triangular: primero los triángulos, luego los rectángulos y luego un total final.
Ordénalo como si armaras una plantilla: el área de un triángulo, duplicarla, el área de cada rectángulo, sumar los rectángulos y combinar todo.
Coloca 'Halla el área de una base triangular' primero: necesitas un triángulo antes de poder duplicarlo.

approaching.label: Match each solid to its description.
approaching.hint: Match each solid to its description of faces and units.
hints: Read each card: some describe face counts, some describe units, and one describes a flat fold-out pattern.
Match by counting: cubes and rectangular prisms have 6 faces; a triangular prism has 5. Units: ² for surfaces, ³ for filling.
Start with 'Net' — it's the 2D pattern that folds into a 3D shape. Then match each solid to its face count.
approaching.explanation: The matches come from counting faces and reading units: a rectangular prism and a cube both have 6 faces (the cube's are 6 identical squares), a triangular prism has 5 (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), a net is the flat 2D pattern that folds into the solid, and surface area is measured in square units (in²) while volume uses cubic units (in³).
approaching.explanationEs: Las parejas salen de contar caras y leer las unidades: un prisma rectangular y un cubo tienen 6 caras (las del cubo son 6 cuadrados idénticos), un prisma triangular tiene 5 (2 triángulos + 3 rectángulos), una red es el patrón plano en 2D que se dobla para formar el sólido, y el área de superficie se mide en unidades cuadradas (in²) mientras que el volumen usa unidades cúbicas (in³).
approaching.labelEs: Une cada sólido con su descripción.
hintsEs: Lee cada tarjeta: algunas describen conteos de caras, otras describen unidades y una describe un patrón plano que se dobla.
Empareja contando: los cubos y los prismas rectangulares tienen 6 caras; un prisma triangular tiene 5. Unidades: ² para superficies y ³ para llenar.
Empieza con 'Plantilla': es el patrón 2D que se dobla en una figura 3D. Luego une cada sólido con su conteo de caras.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake — A Forgotten Face

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: Rectangular prism time capsule: l = 5 in, w = 3 in, h = 2 in.
workedExample.workEs: Cápsula del tiempo de prisma rectangular: l = 5 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 2 pulg.

approaching.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply the last face pair (3×2) by 2. It should be 2(3×2) = 12, not 6. Correct: SA = 30 + 20 + 12 = 62 in².
hints: A prism has 6 faces, in 3 matching pairs — every pair gets multiplied by 2.
The last term should be 2(3×2) = 12, not 6. Correct SA = 30 + 20 + 12 = 62 in².
approaching.titleEs: Descubre el error común — una cara olvidada
approaching.explanation: In the Calculate step the student doubled the first two face pairs but wrote (3×2) = 6 for the last one. A rectangular prism has 6 faces in 3 matching pairs, so that term must be 2(3×2) = 12, giving SA = 30 + 20 + 12 = 62 in².
approaching.explanationEs: En el paso de calcular, el estudiante duplicó los dos primeros pares de caras, pero escribió (3×2) = 6 para el último. Un prisma rectangular tiene 6 caras en 3 pares iguales, así que ese término debe ser 2(3×2) = 12, lo que da SA = 30 + 20 + 12 = 62 in².
approaching.correctWorkEs: El estudiante olvidó multiplicar el último par de caras (3×2) por 2. Debe ser 2(3×2) = 12, no 6. Correcto: SA = 30 + 20 + 12 = 62 in².

onLevel.instructions: Calculate the surface area of each rectangular prism time capsule.
onLevel.hint: Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh for each row: add all six face areas.
hints: Each capsule needs SURFACE AREA: the sum of all six face areas, written in square units.
Row by row, use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh — double each of the three different faces, then add.
Capsule E: the faces are 12×8 = 96, 12×5 = 60, and 8×5 = 40. Double each, then add the three results.
onLevel.explanation: Each capsule is wrapped on all six faces, so use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh. Capsule E gives 2(96) + 2(60) + 2(40) = 392 in², Capsule F gives 2(54) + 2(54) + 2(36) = 288 cm², and Capsule G gives 2(60) + 2(45) + 2(12) = 234 ft² — and each answer keeps the square units of its row.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada cápsula se envuelve por sus seis caras, así que usa SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh. La cápsula E da 2(96) + 2(60) + 2(40) = 392 in², la cápsula F da 2(54) + 2(54) + 2(36) = 288 cm² y la cápsula G da 2(60) + 2(45) + 2(12) = 234 ft², y cada respuesta conserva las unidades cuadradas de su fila.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Calcula el área superficial de cada cápsula del tiempo con forma de prisma rectangular.
hintsEs: Cada cápsula necesita el ÁREA SUPERFICIAL: la suma de las seis áreas de cara, escrita en unidades cuadradas.
Fila por fila, usa AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah: duplica cada una de las tres caras distintas y luego suma.
Cápsula E: las caras son 12×8 = 96, 12×5 = 60 y 8×5 = 40. Duplica cada una y luego suma los tres resultados.

onLevel.stem: A triangular prism has triangular bases with base 6 in and height 4 in. The prism is 10 in long and the two slant sides of the triangle are each 5 in. What is the surface area?
onLevel.explanation: Triangular bases: 2 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 24 in². Three rectangular faces: 6(10) + 5(10) + 5(10) = 60 + 50 + 50 = 160 in². SA = 24 + 160 = 184 in².
choiceFeedback: You added the three rectangular faces but left out the two triangular bases.
You added the two slanted rectangular faces and the bases but missed the bottom rectangular face.
Check the units — a wrapped surface is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Gather the parts: two triangle bases (base 6 in, height 4 in) and three rectangles, each 10 in long.
SA = 2 triangle areas + 3 rectangle areas. Each rectangle is one triangle side (6, 5, or 5) times the 10 in length.
Triangles first: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, doubled is 24 in². Then find the rectangles: 6 × 10, 5 × 10, and 5 × 10.
onLevel.stemEs: Un prisma triangular tiene bases triangulares con base 6 in y altura 4 in. El prisma mide 10 in de largo y los dos lados inclinados del triángulo miden 5 in cada uno. ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
onLevel.explanationEs: Bases triangulares: 2 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 24 in². Tres caras rectangulares: 6(10) + 5(10) + 5(10) = 60 + 50 + 50 = 160 in². Área de superficie = 24 + 160 = 184 in².
hintsEs: Reúne las partes: dos bases triangulares (base 6 pulg, altura 4 pulg) y tres rectángulos, cada uno de 10 pulg de largo.
AS = 2 áreas de triángulo + 3 áreas de rectángulo. Cada rectángulo es un lado del triángulo (6, 5 o 5) por el largo de 10 pulg.
Los triángulos primero: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, duplicado son 24 pulg². Luego halla los rectángulos: 6 × 10, 5 × 10 y 5 × 10.

onLevel.label: A rectangular prism has SA = 340 cm². The top/bottom pair = 150 cm². The front/back pair = 120 cm². Find the left/right pair.
onLevel.questionText: What is the combined area of the left and right faces?
onLevel.hint: Subtract the face areas you already know from the total surface area.
hints: The total SA of 340 cm² splits into three pairs. Top/bottom = 150 cm² and front/back = 120 cm² are known.
Whatever the two known pairs don't cover must be the left/right pair — subtract them from the total.
Add the known pairs: 150 + 120 = 270 cm². Then find the gap between 270 and 340.
onLevel.explanation: The whole bar is the total surface area of 340 cm², and it is made of three face pairs. The two known pairs cover 150 + 120 = 270 cm², so the left/right pair must fill the rest: 340 − 270 = 70 cm².
onLevel.explanationEs: La barra completa es el área de superficie total de 340 cm², y está formada por tres pares de caras. Los dos pares conocidos cubren 150 + 120 = 270 cm², así que el par izquierdo/derecho debe cubrir el resto: 340 − 270 = 70 cm².

onLevel.label: Sort these prisms from LEAST surface area to GREATEST.

categories.label: Least → Greatest surface area
categories.labelEs: De menor → a mayor área de superficie

onLevel.hint: Compare each shape's surface area and order them.
hints: Every card shows its SA after the equals sign, like 'Cube 3×3×3: SA = 54'. Sort by those numbers.
Compare only the SA values from least to greatest — the dimensions are just labels here.
Pick the card with the smallest SA value first, then keep choosing the next smallest.
onLevel.explanation: Each card already states its surface area, so ordering the cards just means ordering those numbers: 54, then 94, then 158, then 248. The cube 3×3×3 has the least surface area and the 10×6×4 prism has the greatest, because bigger dimensions create bigger faces to cover.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta ya indica su área de superficie, así que ordenar las tarjetas es ordenar esos números: 54, luego 94, luego 158 y luego 248. El cubo de 3×3×3 tiene la menor área de superficie y el prisma de 10×6×4 la mayor, porque unas dimensiones más grandes crean caras más grandes que cubrir.
onLevel.labelEs: Ordena estos prismas del MENOR área superficial al MAYOR.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta muestra su AS después del signo igual, como 'Cubo 3×3×3: AS = 54'. Clasifica por esos números.
Compara solo los valores de AS de menor a mayor: las dimensiones aquí son solo etiquetas.
Elige primero la tarjeta con el AS menor y luego sigue eligiendo el siguiente más pequeño.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake — Surface Area or Volume?

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: Rectangular prism time capsule: l = 7 in, w = 4 in, h = 3 in. Find the surface area.
workedExample.workEs: Cápsula del tiempo de prisma rectangular: l = 7 pulg, a = 4 pulg, h = 3 pulg. Encuentra el área superficial.

workedExample.label: Formula
workedExample.work: Surface area adds all 6 faces: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh.
workedExample.workEs: El área superficial suma las 6 caras: SA = 2la + 2lh + 2ah.

workedExample.label: Calculate
workedExample.work: The student multiplied the three dimensions: 7 × 4 × 3 = 84, so they wrote SA = 84 in².
workedExample.workEs: El estudiante multiplicó las tres dimensiones: 7 × 4 × 3 = 84, así que escribió SA = 84 in².

onLevel.correctWork: Multiplying l × w × h gives the VOLUME (84 in³), not surface area. Add all six faces: SA = 2(7×4) + 2(7×3) + 2(4×3) = 56 + 42 + 24 = 122 in².
hints: l × w × h fills the inside (volume, cubic units). Surface area covers the outside.
onLevel.titleEs: Descubre el error común — ¿área de superficie o volumen?
onLevel.explanation: In the Calculate step the student multiplied 7 × 4 × 3, which fills the inside of the box — that is volume, 84 in³, not surface area. Surface area covers the outside, so add all six faces: 2(7×4) + 2(7×3) + 2(4×3) = 56 + 42 + 24 = 122 in².
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso de calcular, el estudiante multiplicó 7 × 4 × 3, lo que llena el interior de la caja: eso es el volumen, 84 in³, no el área de superficie. El área de superficie cubre el exterior, así que suma las seis caras: 2(7×4) + 2(7×3) + 2(4×3) = 56 + 42 + 24 = 122 in².
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Multiplicar l × a × h da el VOLUMEN (84 in³), no el área superficial. Suma las seis caras: SA = 2(7×4) + 2(7×3) + 2(4×3) = 56 + 42 + 24 = 122 in².

extending.title: Find the Surface Area Error

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: Rectangular prism: l = 12 cm, w = 7 cm, h = 5 cm
workedExample.workEs: Prisma rectangular: l = 12 cm, a = 7 cm, h = 5 cm

extending.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply 7 × 5 by 2. It should be 2(7×5) = 2(35) = 70, not 35. Correct: SA = 168 + 120 + 70 = 358 cm².
hints: Check Step 3: did the student multiply every face pair by 2?
2(7×5) = 2(35) = 70, not 35. The student forgot the '2' on the last pair.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de área de superficie
extending.explanation: The Calculate step doubled 12×7 and 12×5 but left 7 × 5 as a single 35, so one whole face was left out. That pair should be 2(7×5) = 70, which makes SA = 168 + 120 + 70 = 358 cm².
extending.explanationEs: El paso de calcular duplicó 12×7 y 12×5, pero dejó 7 × 5 como un solo 35, así que faltó una cara completa. Ese par debe ser 2(7×5) = 70, lo que da SA = 168 + 120 + 70 = 358 cm².
extending.correctWorkEs: El estudiante olvidó multiplicar 7 × 5 por 2. Debe ser 2(7×5) = 2(35) = 70, no 35. Correcto: SA = 168 + 120 + 70 = 358 cm².

extending.prompt: A company ships products in two container options: a rectangular prism (8 × 6 × 4 in) or a triangular prism (triangle base 8 in, triangle height 6 in, prism length 8 in, slant sides 6.3 in each). Both must be wrapped in protective film. Which shape uses LESS film? Show your work.
extending.sentenceFrame: Rectangular prism SA = 2(___) + 2(___) + 2(___) = ___ in². Triangular prism SA = 2(___) + ___ + ___ + ___ = ___ in². The ___ uses less film because ___.
extending.hint: Find the surface area of each shape, then compare which uses less film.
hints: Both containers get wrapped, so compare SURFACE AREAS. Collect each shape's faces before calculating.
Rect prism: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh. Tri prism: 2 triangle bases + 3 rectangles (each side length × the 8 in length).
Rect prism first: faces are 8×6 = 48, 8×4 = 32, 6×4 = 24. Double each and add, then tackle the triangular prism.
extending.explanation: Film covers the outside, so compare surface areas. The rectangular prism gives 2(8×6) + 2(8×4) + 2(6×4) = 96 + 64 + 48 = 208 in², while the triangular prism gives two triangles 2(½ × 8 × 6) = 48 plus three rectangles 8×8 = 64 and two of 6.3×8 = 50.4, for 212.8 in². The rectangular container uses less film, by about 4.8 in².
extending.explanationEs: La película cubre el exterior, así que compara las áreas de superficie. El prisma rectangular da 2(8×6) + 2(8×4) + 2(6×4) = 96 + 64 + 48 = 208 in², mientras que el prisma triangular da dos triángulos 2(½ × 8 × 6) = 48 más tres rectángulos: 8×8 = 64 y dos de 6.3×8 = 50.4, para un total de 212.8 in². El recipiente rectangular usa menos película, por unas 4.8 in².
extending.promptEs: Una compañía envía productos en dos opciones de recipiente: un prisma rectangular (8 × 6 × 4 in) o un prisma triangular (base del triángulo 8 in, altura del triángulo 6 in, largo del prisma 8 in, lados inclinados de 6.3 in cada uno). Los dos deben envolverse con película protectora. ¿Cuál forma usa MENOS película? Muestra tu trabajo.
hintsEs: Ambos recipientes se envuelven, así que compara ÁREAS SUPERFICIALES. Reúne las caras de cada figura antes de calcular.
Prisma rectangular: AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah. Prisma triangular: 2 bases triangulares + 3 rectángulos (cada lado por el largo de 8 pulg).
Prisma rectangular primero: las caras son 8×6 = 48, 8×4 = 32 y 6×4 = 24. Duplica cada una y suma; luego resuelve el prisma triangular.

extending.instructions: A rectangular prism and a triangular prism have similar dimensions. Compare their surface areas and volumes.
rows: Tri prism: base=6, h=4, length=3, sides=5
extending.hint: For each shape, find both the surface area and the volume.
hints: Two shapes, four blanks: each needs a surface area and a volume. The tri prism's triangle has base 6 and height 4.
Rect prism: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh, V = l × w × h. Tri prism: SA = 2 triangles + 3 rectangles; V = triangle area × length.
Rect prism first: faces 6×4 = 24, 6×3 = 18, 4×3 = 12 — double and add for SA; then multiply 6 × 4 × 3 for volume.
extending.explanation: For the 6×4×3 rectangular prism, SA = 2(24) + 2(18) + 2(12) = 108 and V = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72. For the triangular prism, the triangle area is ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, so SA = 2(12) + (6×3) + (5×3) + (5×3) = 24 + 48 = 72 and V = 12 × 3 = 36. Both of the triangular prism's measures are half the rectangular prism's because its base is half the rectangle's base.
extending.explanationEs: Para el prisma rectangular de 6×4×3, SA = 2(24) + 2(18) + 2(12) = 108 y V = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72. Para el prisma triangular, el área del triángulo es ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, así que SA = 2(12) + (6×3) + (5×3) + (5×3) = 24 + 48 = 72 y V = 12 × 3 = 36. Las dos medidas del prisma triangular son la mitad de las del prisma rectangular porque su base es la mitad de la base del rectángulo.
extending.instructionsEs: Un prisma rectangular y un prisma triangular tienen dimensiones parecidas. Compara sus áreas superficiales y sus volúmenes.
hintsEs: Dos figuras, cuatro espacios: cada una necesita un área superficial y un volumen. El triángulo del prisma triangular tiene base 6 y altura 4.
Prisma rectangular: AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah, V = l × a × h. Prisma triangular: AS = 2 triángulos + 3 rectángulos; V = área del triángulo × largo.
Prisma rectangular primero: caras 6×4 = 24, 6×3 = 18, 4×3 = 12 — duplica y suma para el AS; luego multiplica 6 × 4 × 3 para el volumen.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Surface Area of Prisms is confusing surface area with volume — multiplying l × w × h (which finds the space INSIDE the prism, in cubic units) instead of adding the areas of all the faces (SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh, in square units). A second common slip is forgetting to double one face pair, like writing 2(l×w) + 2(l×h) + (w×h) instead of + 2(w×h) — always count all 6 faces (or all 5 for a triangular prism) before you submit.

connect.scenario: A carpenter builds wooden storage chests. A rectangular chest is 3 feet long, 2 feet wide, and 2 feet tall. Wood stain covers 50 square feet per can.
connect.promptQuestion: How much surface area needs staining, and how many cans of stain are needed?

check.stem: What is the chest's surface area?
How many cans of stain are needed for one chest?
check.explanation: 32 ÷ 50 = 0.64, so one can (which covers 50 ft²) is more than enough.

check.stem: The carpenter builds a second identical chest. Now how many cans?
check.explanation: Two chests need 2 × 32 = 64 ft². Since 64 ÷ 50 = 1.28, one can is not enough — you need 2.

connect.modelAnswer: SA = 2(3 × 2) + 2(3 × 2) + 2(2 × 2) = 12 + 12 + 8 = 32 ft². One can covers 50 ft², and 32 ÷ 50 = 0.64, so 1 can is enough.

exitTicket.stem: A rectangular prism has l = 8 ft, w = 6 ft, h = 3 ft. What is the surface area?
exitTicket.explanation: SA = 2(8×6) + 2(8×3) + 2(6×3) = 96 + 48 + 36 = 180 ft². Surface area uses square units (ft²).
choiceFeedback: 144 is the volume — surface area sums all six faces.
Surface area uses square units (ft²), not cubic.
You found only three faces — each face has a matching pair.
hints: You want the surface area of an 8 × 6 × 3 prism: all six faces added, in square units (ft²).
Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh — three different face areas, each counted twice.
Faces first: 8×6 = 48, 8×3 = 24, and 6×3 = 18. Double each area, then add the three results.
